questions.question: Categorize process management commands into monitoring and controlling tools, and justify your classification with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Categorize process management commands into monitoring and controlling tools. Monitoring Commands:
  • • ps
  • • top
  • • pgrep Controlling Commands:
  • • kill
  • • killall
  • • nice
  • • renice Justification: Monitoring commands observe process status, whereas controlling commands manage or terminate processes.

questions.question: Explain how Linux differentiates access rights between file owners, groups, and others.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how Linux differentiates access rights between owners, groups, and others. Linux permissions are divided into:
  • • Owner (u): Creator of the file.
  • • Group (g): Members of the assigned group.
  • • Others (o): All other users. Permissions:
  • • Read (r)
  • • Write (w)
  • • Execute (x) Example:
  • -rwxr-xr--
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: -rwxr-xr

  • • Original UNIX shell.
  • • Supports scripting. Bash Shell (bash)
  • • Default Linux shell.
  • • Command history, aliases, job control. C Shell (csh)

  • • Command completion and editing. Z Shell (zsh)

  • • Advanced completion and themes.

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of managing users and groups separately in Linux. Explain how this separation improves system security and simplifies administration in multi-user environments.
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the effectiveness of managing users and groups separately in Linux.
  • Managing users and groups separately improves:
  • Security
  • • Access control based on user roles.
  • • Restricts unauthorized access.
  • Simplified Administration
  • • Permissions can be assigned to groups rather than individual users.
  • • Easier management of large organizations.
  • Resource Sharing
  • • Group members can share files and resources efficiently.
  • Scalability
  • • New users can be added to existing groups quickly.
  • Accountability
  • • User activities can be tracked individually.
  • Conclusion: Separate management of users and groups enhances security, flexibility, scalability,
  • and administrative efficiency in multi-user Linux environments.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: and administrative efficiency in multi-user Linux environments.
